entries.detail: Rule DI-002 requires stopping and disclosing when a real result is unavailable, rather than substituting fake/old data or papering over gaps; SUBJECT is 'the work product produced this session', so per task instructions I audited it against the only written record available, /Users/scottlydon/Developer/GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md (356 lines, read in full). Also ran a targeted grep for assum/infer/presum/cached/stale/carried-over language to catch undisclosed substitutions. Every instance found is the document explicitly disclosing a substitution or a blocked gap rather than hiding one: the 'What blocks Phase 1' section (lines 45-56) stops and states a real Amazon reader session is unavailable rather than faking one; item 3.3 (lines 345-356) leaves an item unticked and explains a branch does not exist rather than cutting a cosmetic one after the fact; item 9.4 and Z.4 (lines 105-111, 250-253) disclose a method substitution (reading files directly instead of spawning an agent) by name; item 3.2 (lines 340-343) discloses that the entitlements check ran against a freshly migrated database rather than $DATABASE_URL because none is exported, and explains why that still answers the question; item 4.13 (lines 322-330) records a harness finding where a suite silently reported success on 0 executed tests, and states the fix used to make the following run real rather than accepting the false pass. No line in the file presents an inferred, filled-in, or old result as if it were a fresh success without disclosure. This is the only account of the session available to me per the task's own instruction, so I cannot independently verify mtimes of the artifacts it references, but on the written record itself the rule holds.
entries.rule_title: Stop and say so when a real result is unavailable

entries.detail: Ran the deterministic pattern `rg -n -i '(cost|dollars|latency|tokens|count|score|percent|duration|total|spent|rating)\s*[:=]\s*(0|0\.0|-1|999)'` against all five targets (Migrations dir, Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, Questionnaire.swift). One hit: /Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/NotificationDispatcher.swift:58 `var recipientCount = -1`. Read the full function (lines 1-97): the -1 is never surfaced as a real count. It exists only to distinguish "recipient read itself failed" from a genuine zero, and line 79 converts it to the string "unknown" before it reaches any log line (`recipientCount < 0 ? "unknown" : "\(recipientCount)"`) - the surrounding comment (lines 76-77) explicitly states this is to avoid the number claiming zero subscribers. It never reaches a user-facing aggregate (no sum/avg/chart/total column) and never propagates as a fabricated measurement, so it does not violate the rule's crime (a default value silently standing in for a real measurement in a user-facing aggregate) - it is the correct "not-yet-measured" signal pattern the rule itself prescribes as the fix, applied to a log string rather than a numeric field consumers read as data. A broader unfiltered grep for count/score/percent/total/avg/rating/tokens assignments across the same targets (second command) surfaced no other numeric-literal assignments to check. No other cost/latency/score/percent/rating/duration/spent fields exist in these targets at all (grep found zero hits for those terms outside NotificationDispatcher.swift and two unrelated `.count` property reads in ProfileResolver.swift/ProfileService.swift, which are live collection counts, not stored defaults).
entries.rule_title: Numbers in user-facing aggregates are real measurements, never defaults

entries.detail: Rule targets aggregators (sum/avg/min/max/percent) over nullable numeric fields that coerce null to zero instead of excluding it. Searched all five target paths with rg for the deterministic pattern (or 0|?? 0|coalesce|fillna(0)|default: 0) and for sum/average/reduce/count/percent usage: zero matches for the null-coercion patterns; the only reduce/count calls found (Matchmaking/ProfileActivation.swift:106,188, Subscriptions/SubscriptionService.swift:140,146, Models/Migrations/CreateGreetUserSettings.swift:45,57, Subscriptions/NotificationFanOut.swift:161) are dictionary-building or SQL EventLoopFuture chaining, not numeric aggregation over a nullable measurement field. Models/Questionnaire.swift and AuthorVisibility/*.swift contain no scoring/averaging aggregation code at all (the only 'score' hit is an unrelated comment at Questionnaire.swift:12). No dashboard-style cost/measurement aggregation exists in these targets, so the rule's subject (an aggregator conflating absent-measurement with measured-zero) has nothing to attach to here.
entries.rule_title: Aggregators treat None as absent, not as zero
